phan_vu: Phần Vũ Đường, body cultivators of the vent country: bare arms, always with a wide red sash of heavy cloth; men in sleeveless dark-red or undyed vests, women in sleeveless red; every sitting leaves a pale line of scar from wrist to shoulder, so elders' arms are white with fine lines; the cloth is clean and well made, plain not ragged; a lone small red feather ornament for the head; servants wear brown cotton without the sash.
ho_lam: Hộ Lâm Đường, forest wardens of the northern woods: long coats of bark-brown wool waxed to a faint sheen, wooden toggles, a green sash or green cord; hornet-veil hats of coarse straw with black gauze in summer; an axe on the back or a coil of tally cord; raftsmen go barefoot with trousers rolled; clean, sturdy, well fitted, plain but not worn.
hoa_cai: Hoa Cái Đường, a pill house of the badlands: vermilion coats of fine or waxed cloth with stiff standing collars, darker red sashes and pale collars; thin gloves of oiled yellow silk; leather masks with round glass eyes in the mercury room (hung at the neck or held when off); the refined are crisp and clean, washers' coats stained rust-red at the cuffs; no writing on any cloth.
